video_title: Shocking Contracts: Wemby Gives Back Money To Help Spurs Pursue Titles + Bucks’ Bold Deal

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama's contract extension lacks the 'Rose provision' to maximize team flexibility
quotes.excerpt: It does not have the escalator in it, what we call the Rose provision.
quotes.quote: Victor Wembanyama agreed to five years and 250 million. It is a great contract, but it does not have the escalator in it, what we call the Rose provision, which means if he had won the MVP award, won the Defensive Player of the Year again, or made the All-NBA team in this upcoming season, he would have gotten the bump from 25% of the cap to 30% of the cap. That is going to be worth potentially 53 million dollars, somewhere in the neighborhood of 10 plus million dollars a year.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's contract extension provides the Spurs with significant financial flexibility
quotes.excerpt: It does not create cap space, but it does create significant flexibility in this apron era.
quotes.quote: It does not create cap space, but it does create significant flexibility in this apron era where the second apron is so dreaded. And it is a partnership. You do not just give a discount from the bottom of your heart and out of kindness. You give a discount and the deal is, I will take the 25% and I will take less if you promise that you are going to maintain a championship-caliber supporting cast around me. That is the partnership. That is the promise from the Spurs.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: NBPA executive director David Kelly criticizes the second apron's impact on team decisions
quotes.excerpt: We are seeing the apron system decimate teams and force decisions to be made that are not basketball decisions.
quotes.quote: We are not fans of the second apron. We did not propose the second apron. We should have done a better job of fighting back against the second apron. In the future, we will have a much more unified union, and we will do a better job of fighting back. We are seeing the apron system decimate teams and force decisions to be made that are not basketball decisions.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon proposes a boxing match to settle player disputes during Summer League
quotes.excerpt: In a case like this, what Bam does is he challenges Tyler Herro to a boxing match.
quotes.quote: In a case like this, what Bam does is he challenges Tyler Herro to a boxing match. If, for example, Jaylen Brown feels a certain sort of way about Jason Tatum as he is kind of hinted, he could challenge Jason Tatum to a boxing match. These would be done at halftime when their teams meet during Summer League. I have done some further thinking, as I am a deep thinker. Not only would it boost ticket sales, but we would still have the normal halftime show on TV and then you would have the pay-per-view.

quotes.speaker: Brian Windhorst
quotes.summary_phrase: Gary Trent Jr.'s minimum contract with the Bucks is a surprising value move
quotes.excerpt: The Bucks got him on a minimum contract, which was a surprise.
quotes.quote: The Bucks got him on a minimum contract, which was a surprise. A lot of people were surprised that the Bucks got him on a minimum contract. And he then again, he averaged 11 points and shot 42% from threes and he played 70-something games. That is a production that should probably get you around eight figures, do not you think?

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: MacMahon criticizes Gary Trent Jr.'s recent performance and contract value
quotes.excerpt: If you look at the analytics of it, he had negative win shares, a negative box plus-minus.
quotes.quote: If you look at the analytics of it, he had negative win shares, a negative box plus-minus, a negative VORP, and he got a mid-level exception basically, a full mid-level. Come on, Brian. This contract stinks. It smells awful.

quotes.speaker: Tim MacMahon
quotes.summary_phrase: Pelicans' decision to give DeAndre Jordan a fully guaranteed minimum contract is questionable
quotes.excerpt: The New Orleans Pelicans giving DeAndre Jordan a fully guaranteed two-year minimum, which, listen, you want DeAndre Jordan.
quotes.quote: The New Orleans Pelicans giving DeAndre Jordan a fully guaranteed two-year minimum, which, listen, you want DeAndre Jordan to be your vet mentor for the next two years, cool. The problem is when you give him a fully guaranteed two-year minimum, you do not get the savings that come with giving a guy a minimum. So basically, you just burn three million dollars over two years. If it is a one plus a team option, you get the savings. Certainly a one-year deal.
